title: Construction of Sets of Orthogonal Quantum States with Minimal Nonlocality in Bipartite and Tripartite Systems of Unequal Local Dimensions
authors: Ben-Hao Zhao, Dong-Huan Jiang, Yu-Guang Yang, Guang-Bao Xu
abstract: The research on minimal nonlocality aims to determine the minimal cardinality of nonlocal sets of quantum states. However, the construction of a nonlocal set of states in bipartite or tripartite quantum systems with unequal local dimensions remains unsolved. In this paper, we first give a method to construct a set of orthogonal quantum states with minimal nonlocality in $\mathbb{C}^{4} \otimes \mathbb{C}^{7}$ quantum system. Then we give a general method to construct a set of orthogonal quantum states with minimal nonlocality in a bipartite quantum system with unequal local dimensions. Furthermore, we generalize the construction method to tripartite quantum system with unequal local dimensions, and construct a set of orthogonal quantum states with minimal nonlocality in $\mathbb C^{d_1} \otimes \mathbb C^{d_2}\otimes \mathbb C^{d_3}$ quantum system for $5\le d_1 < d_2 < d_3$. Our work settles the construction problem of a set of orthogonal states with minimal nonlocality in both bipartite and tripartite systems with unequal local dimensions.
summary: This paper develops general methods to construct sets of orthogonal quantum states exhibiting minimal nonlocality in both bipartite and tripartite quantum systems with unequal local dimensions. The authors prove that removing any single state from the set allows for perfect distinguishability via LOCC, while the full set resists such distinction. This settles a long-standing construction problem in quantum information theory.
main_problem: The research aims to determine the minimal cardinality of nonlocal sets of orthogonal quantum states, specifically for bipartite and tripartite systems with unequal local dimensions.
main_result: The authors successfully provide general construction methods that settle the problem of finding such sets in both bipartite ($	ext{C}_{d_1} \otimes 	ext{C}_{d_2}$) and tripartite ($	ext{C}_{d_1} \otimes 	ext{C}_{d_2} \otimes 	ext{C}_{d_3}$) systems with unequal local dimensions.
method: The methodology involves constructing specific sets of orthogonal states and then proving minimal nonlocality by analyzing the conditions under which subsets of these states remain perfectly distinguishable via Local Operations and Classical Communication (LOCC).
model_or_system: The study focuses on quantum systems described by tensor products of Hilbert spaces, specifically $	ext{C}_{d_1} \otimes 	ext{C}_{d_2}$ (bipartite) and $	ext{C}_{d_1} \otimes 	ext{C}_{d_2} \otimes 	ext{C}_{d_3}$ (tripartite), where the local dimensions ($d_i$) are unequal.
key_observables: Minimal nonlocality, distinguishability via LOCC, and the structure of measurement operators ($\{M^\dagger_{AMA}\}$ or $\{M^\dagger_{BMB}\}$).
important_parameters: The local dimensions $d_1, d_2, d_3$, and the specific indices defining the states within the set.
main_assumptions: The proofs rely on analyzing orthogonality conditions derived from assuming the existence of LOCC measurements that preserve state orthogonality.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates the structure of a minimal nonlocal set in $	ext{C}_4 \otimes 	ext{C}_7$. Figures 2 and 3 illustrate the structures of sets $S_2$ and $S_3$, respectively, in bipartite and tripartite spaces.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first solving the problem for a specific case ($	ext{C}_4 \otimes 	ext{C}_7$), then generalizing the construction method to arbitrary unequal-dimensional bipartite systems, and finally extending this generalization to tripartite quantum systems.
why_interesting: This work provides rigorous mathematical tools for characterizing fundamental resource properties (nonlocality) in multipartite quantum systems, which is crucial for understanding communication complexity and security protocols.
